title: Debias It Yourself: Teaching LLMs Cognitive Bias-Mitigation Interventions
measurement_description: The paper measures cognitive bias mitigation in LLMs across 9 demographic dimensions, including religion, using five psychological interventions (e.g., Stereotype Replacement, Counter-Stereotypical Imaging). It evaluates bias scores as the absolute distance from an unbiased baseline using likelihood, multiple-choice, and open-ended generation metrics.
findings: The study found that applying cognitively-grounded bias mitigation interventions successfully reduced bias against religious groups (along with other demographic categories) without degrading general reasoning performance. Additionally, bias reduction generalized across dimensions: models trained to reduce bias on gender or other source dimensions successfully transferred this capability to reduce bias on unseen dimensions, including religion, and vice versa.
references: Gordon W. Allport. 1954. The Nature of Prejudice. Addison-Wesley.
